svg.title: Conditional Bernoulli repair of a compact-extraction seed
svg.desc: Theorem 3.23 requires a separable compact Hausdorff seed with a fully supported probability, a conull standard Borel carrier whose compact subsets are null, and finite-power Borel equality. The product-Borel gate makes the actual countable carrier measurable and standard. Mixing of the shift and Fourier coefficients prove ergodicity after an irrational circle rotation. That rotation is free on every ambient point. Compact subsets project into null compact seed subsets. Theorem 3.23 is conditional; Proposition 3.28 realizes its complete seed under CH.
svg.text: An ergodic repair, conditional on the complete seed
Theorem 3.23 · actual inherited topology throughout
All five seed hypotheses
K separable compact Hausdorff; ν a fully supported Borel probability
Y ⊂ K Borel, ν(Y) = 1; the relative Borel space Y is standard
C ⊂ Y compact ⇒ ν(C) = 0
For every finite r: B(Yʳ) = B(Y) ⊗ ··· ⊗ B(Y) [r factors]
Product-Borel gate · Lemma 3.21
Finite coordinate sets are countable in number; circle arcs have a countable base.
Hence B(Yℤ × T) equals the coordinate sigma-algebra. T = R / ℤ.
The actual space, carrier, measure and action
X = Kℤ × T; E = Yℤ × T; μ = ι*(ηℤ ⊗ ℓ); η = ν|Y
T(x, z) = (σx, z + α); (σx)ⱼ = xⱼ₊₁; α irrational; ℓ circle length
X compact and separable; E Borel, conull and standard; μ invariant and fully supported
Ergodicity · Theorem 3.23
Disjoint finite coordinates ⇒ mixing.
Invariant F: Fₘ ∘ σ = e−2πimα Fₘ.
m ≠ 0 ⇒ Fₘ = 0; F₀ constant.
Circle Fourier completeness ⇒ F constant.
Freeness and compact obstruction
Tⁿ(x, z) = (x, z) ⇒ nα ∈ ℤ ⇒ n = 0.
L ⊂ E compact → π₀(L) ⊂ Y compact.
Free on every X point; no minimality claim.
The complete seed is realized under CH below
Single-factor standardness does not prove the finite-power Borel condition.
Theorem 3.27 verifies all finite powers; Proposition 3.28 supplies the seed.
This diagram gives the reduction; Theorem 3.29 gives its CH realization.
Proof locators: (3.35)–(3.38) gate; (3.41), (3.48)–(3.49) ergodicity; (3.50) compact mass.

a.text: Human source: Takesaki, Theory of Operator Algebras III, XIII.1, Exercise 5(a), pp. 11–12.
